title: ZhiPu ZCode Launches New Compensation Round: Gifts 8 Reset Cards to Paid Users, Completely Removes Code Snapshot Upload Pipeline
excerpt: Intellifusion's AI coding tool ZCode officially launched a new user compensation plan on September 28th to address previous controversies over code data uploads
content_html:
Intellifusion's AI coding tool ZCode officially launched a new user compensation plan on September 28th to address previous controversies over code data uploads, and disclosed progress on technical security improvements to rebuild developer trust.

According to the official announcement, the compensation measures took effect at 10:30 AM on September 28th. Paid users and those who returned within one month will receive 4 weekly quotas and 4 5-hour quota reset cards, valid for one month; meanwhile, during the period from September 28th to October 7th, the platform will distribute "100 million Tokens × 100,000 copies" daily to all users.

In the capital market, affected by previous incidents, Intellifusion's shares opened lower on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on the 28th, with a price of HKD 620.5 per share, down 2.05%.

Regarding the technical chain vulnerability, the official confirmed that the repository snapshot upload path has been completely removed, and cloud-stored data has been verified by a third party and fully deleted. The company has pledged that code will remain entirely local except for user-initiated operations.

The incident began on September 18th, when the "Code Repository Index" feature in ZCode triggered data uploads by default when generating Repo Wiki pages, sparking controversy. Intellifusion subsequently implemented function fixes, product open-sourcing, and introduced third-party security audits.

Currently, AI coding intelligences are accelerating their penetration into production environments, and edge-side privacy protection has become an absolute red line for enterprise-level deployment. This shift from default cloud synchronization to pure local indexing and transparent governance marks a transformation in the competition for AI developer tools—from a single model capability battle to a comprehensive contest of data sovereignty and engineering security infrastructure.
